properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The shared comm-go crypto library defaults to AES-ECB: DEFAULT_CIPHER_MODE = "ECB" (aes.go:21) is what NewAESCipher assigns, Encrypt() supports ONLY the ECB branch (:41), and decryptECB (:52) manually block-encrypts with zero padding. Worse, generateKey() XOR-folds any caller-supplied key down to a fixed 16 bytes, so every consumer gets AES-128-ECB regardless of intended key length. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The execution-factory token test helper generates 1024-bit RSA keypairs (PyCryptodome RSA.generate(1024)) at two points to exercise the token/RSA-PKCS1v15 flow. 1024-bit RSA is factorable with classical hardware today, so even as test scaffolding these keys give no security margin; they also signal the token service under test is RSA-based. Test-only, changeable here — bump to 2048+ or better migrate the underlying scheme to ML-KEM/ML-DSA.

Available in the library, not invoked by the application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: comm-go's decryptCBC uses cipher.NewCBCDecrypter(block, key[:blockSize]) — the IV is the first block of the KEY itself, not a fresh random IV. Unauthenticated CBC (no MAC) plus a key-derived deterministic IV: the same key prefix serves as both key material and IV, which both leaks key structure across messages and makes identical plaintexts produce identical ciphertext. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SM3 in the vendored Kingbase (gokb) database driver, conn.go:2859 — part of the driver's SCRAM-style authentication exchange for KingbaseES (Chinese national-standard DB), keyed with the connection password.
